newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts penned in by 110-00 on upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts penned in by 110-00 on upside.

text.p: June gilts will be confined to a narrow range on Wednesday, penned in by initial resistance at 109-21 ahead of a stronger barrier at 110-00 to 110-03, technical analysts said.
And with the British election looming, they are unlikely to break out of their recent range at least for the remainder of the week, they added.

"The initial target is 109-18,21, a big area of congestion on the charts," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at Monument Derivatives here. By 0729 GMT the June gilt was up 4/32 at 109-17, after falling back from 109-19 earlier.

Ostwald said if the market managed to pierce 109-21 it would encounter another band of thick congestion at 110-00 to 110-03. "That is around the top of the current range between 108-00 and 110-00 -- one which which will persist until the election is over and done with," he said.
Analysts said the British election on May 1 -- widely predicted to result in a victory for the opposition Labour party -- was provoking little excitement in the gilt market.
"Towards the end of next week we might see something happening in gilts, but I don't think this week will push it too hard," said Ostwald.

Ostwald said on the downside, any setback in gilts would find support at 109-04, 08, a series of highs earlier in the month between April 7 and 11. Below there good support at 108-28,29 kicks in, he said.

Juliette Clark at Royal Bank of Scotland, said the June gilt must edge up to resistance at 109-23. "This is the decision level today, the meeting point of the 50 percent retracement of the fall from 110-10 and the expected high," she said.
"A failure to make an impression here will keep the market under pressure and range trading will follow. But a break above 109-23 is another buying signal."
By 0822 GMT June short sterling was unchanged at 93.39.
